s.g: A young plant grown from seed.
A roughly-built hut or cabin.
(biblical) A former kingdom in the Red Sea region. An ancient kingdom in Arabia or possibly in Africa. Frequently equated with ancient Saba.
Any of numerous small, mouselike, chiefly nocturnal, mammals of the family Soricidae.
An ill-tempered, nagging woman: a scold.
Something that silences or (notionally) nearly silences.
One who procrastinates or is lazy; one who does not do their fair share or pull their own weight.
(countable) An artful trick; sly artifice; a feat so dexterous that the manner of performance escapes observation.
A vehicle with skis at the front and a caterpillar track at the rear, used for travelling over snow, sometimes as sport.
With reference to space or arrangement in space.
In a speedy or fast manner.
Expanded polystyrene foam, such as is used in cups and packaging.
(American spelling, chemistry) Of, or relating to sulfur, especially in its higher oxidation state

A fixed or operable opening in a vehicle roof (car or truck) which allows fresh air and/or light to enter the passenger compartment. A sunroof may include a transparent or opaque panel and may be manually operated or power driven.
The capital and largest city of East Java, Indonesia.
The capital city of Estonia.

Any of many (mostly hypothetical or fictional) processes of moving matter from one spatial point to another without physically crossing the space in between and which are often depicted or described as happening instantaneously, and through dematerialization or gateways.
Having a brilliant red colour.
(archaic) To sway back and forth, as if about to fall; to reel, to stagger, to totter.
(military) A belt and shoulder harness with attached pouches used to carry a soldier's equipment, water, ammunition, etc.
Often followed by out: to squeeze or twist (something moist) tightly so that liquid is forced out.
(transitive) To take away by force; to carry away (a human being) wrongfully and usually with violence or deception; to kidnap. [Early 17th century.]
An abundance of wealth.

Any plant in the large, variable genus Agave: succulent plants, commonly armed with formidable prickles; they flower at maturity after several years, and generally die thereafter; large species, such as the maguey or century plant, (Agave americana), produce gigantic inflorescences. Several are of economic importance as sources of fibre such as sisal, and alcoholic beverages such as tequila.
A palace in Granada, Spain; historically a royal palace.
A large city in Punjab, India, formerly known as Ramdaspur and sometimes called Ambarsar.
A periphery where Athens, the capital of Greece, is located.

A musical wind instrument possessing a flexible bag inflated by bellows, a double-reed melody pipe and up to four drone pipes; any aerophone that produces sound using air from a reservoir to vibrate enclosed reeds.

(nautical) A long, narrow strip, originally of wood but now also of fibreglass, metal, etc., used for various purposes aboard a ship; especially one attached to a mast or spar for protection, one holding down the edge of a tarpaulin covering a hatch to prevent water from entering the hatch, one inserted in a pocket sewn on a sail to keep it flat, or one from which a hammock is suspended.
(weaving) The movable bar of a loom, which strikes home or closes the threads of a woof.

(carpentry, construction) A plank or strip of wood, or several of such strips arranged side by side, used in construction to hold members of a structure together, to provide a fixing point, to strengthen, or to prevent warping.
To beg or request for (something).
(figuratively) To attack something or someone by directing objects at them.
Any of the subtribe Tamiina of small, striped rodents; they are found in North America, with the exception of the Siberian chipmunk which is found primarily in Asia.

A sweet or savory but usually spicy condiment, originally from eastern India, made from a variety of fruits and/or vegetables, often containing significant amounts of fresh green or dried red chili peppers. [from 1813]
(figurative) A conclusion (of a statement or event, for example), final portion, tail end.
The examination of the colon using a colonoscope.
The process of bringing peace and harmony; the ending of strife.
The temporary fusion of organisms, especially as part of sexual reproduction.
In some languages, one of several classifications of verbs categorized into distinct classes based on the specific inflectional patterns they exhibit.
(mathematics, logic) A proposition which follows easily from the statement or proof of another proposition.
A force or influence that balances, checks or limits an opposite one.
A native or inhabitant of Czechoslovakia
An act of disrespect or impiety towards something considered sacred.
Instructive or intended to teach or demonstrate, especially with regard to morality.
Teaching from textbooks rather than laboratory demonstration and clinical application.
One who or that which helps something to happen.

A membranous tissue composed of one or more layers of cells which forms the covering of most internal and external surfaces of the body and its organs: internally including the lining of vessels and other small cavities, and externally being the skin.
The science of the design of equipment, especially so as to reduce operator fatigue, discomfort and injury. [from c. 1950.]
Of or relating to a person named Gregory, especially any of the popes of that name.
An estimate, judgment or opinion made by guessing, from limited information.
(electronics) Initialism of hardware description language.

(physiology) The ability of a system or living organism to adjust its internal environment to maintain a state of dynamic constancy; such as the ability of warm-blooded animals to maintain a stable temperature.
A shrub growing this fruit.
A green iguana (Iguana iguana), a large tropical American lizard often kept as a pet.
Incapable of being passed over, crossed, or negotiated.
In an impatient manner.
Insulting in manner or words, particularly in an arrogant or insubordinate manner.
A substance that does not transmit heat (thermal insulator), sound (acoustic insulator) or electricity (electrical insulator).
To turn (something) upside down or inside out; to place in a contrary order or direction.
An animal without vertebrae (i.e., without a backbone).
A chemical element with an atomic number of 77: a very hard, brittle, silvery-white transition metal of the platinum group.
Any device used to jam radio reception.

(historical) The quarter of a town or city inhabited either partially or exclusively by Jews; historically, its main buildings were the synagogue, the ritual bath or mikve, the kosher-oriented butchery and bakery, etc. [from 17th c.]
